about: What may go into Krish's makeyourmindup asset library on Drive, and how a post's folder is named. Krish, 2026-10-06: "I want every single asset in there, permanent and for individual posts, categorized properly, clear what to use them for, and every new post gets its own new folder with all assets including the article HTML I can copy paste, video scripts, etc etc".

Two programs follow this rule: the engine's library routes (apps/control-plane/api/library/_library.ts), which refuse anything else, and the post pack (scripts/post-pack/library.py), which builds and sends the files. Both are tested against every case in this file, so they cannot drift apart. Change the rule here first, then in both.

A library path is relative, with forward slashes, and starts with one of top_folders. Inside "3 Posts" the next folder is one post's folder, and a file in it is either post_readme or sits inside one of post_sections.

Every name is safe on Windows and Google Drive: no . or .. folder, no name starting with a dot, none of < > : " \ | ? * or a control character, no space at either end or dot at the end, none of Windows' reserved device names. Accented letters are written in their composed form (NFC). At most path_max characters in the whole path and part_max in one name, counted as Windows counts them (UTF-16 code units).
The extension decides the type, from content_types; nothing else is taken. A file is at most max_bytes.

A post's folder: YYYY-MM-DD <Day> <subchannel> - <Subject>, with the day the date fell on (Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat or Sun) and the subchannel as the brand writes it; a launch post is YYYY-MM-DD Launch - <Subject>. The subject is made safe by the archive naming rule (config/archive-naming.cases.json) and cut at a space so the whole name stays within part_max.
